{{External|rs|dw=Fight Cave}} {{HasStrategy}} {{Otheruses|the minigame in which players must defeat waves of TzHaar|the minigame in which players fight against each other|TzHaar Fight Pit}} {{Infobox Activity |name = TzHaar Fight Cave |image = [[File:TzHaar Fight Cave.png|300px]] |release = [[4 October]] [[2005]] |update = TzHaar Fight Caves |type = Minigame |members = Yes |location = [[Mor Ul Rek]] |players = 1 |currency = [[Tokkul]] |tutorial = No |music = [[TzHaar!]] |map = {{Map|name=TzHaar Fight Cave|x=2439|y=5172|zoom=3|mapID=23}} |leagueRegion = Karamja }} The '''TzHaar Fight Cave''', commonly referred to as the '''Fight Caves''', is a combat minigame in the outer area of [[Mor Ul Rek]], located within the [[Karamja]] volcano. Fully completing it is considered an early major challenge players will take on in ''Old School RuneScape''. It involves single-handedly fighting off 63 waves of [[volcanic creatures]], including a boss fight against the strongest of the creatures: [[TzTok-Jad]]. Players will be rewarded with [[Tokkul]] for playing this minigame, and if they manage to defeat TzTok-Jad, they will be rewarded with the [[fire cape]]. The Fight Cave was created by the [[TzHaar-Xil]], who use it for practice.{{CiteNPC|npc=TzHaar-Mej-Jal|quote=This is the fight cave, TzHaar-Xil made it for practice, but many JalYt come here to fight too.|loc=|notes=|name=}} {{Listen |title = [[The Fight Continues (Fight Cave)|The Fight Continues]] |align = right |filename = The Fight Continues (Fight Cave).ogg |desc = The jingle that plays upon starting a wave of the Fight Cave.}} ==Transportation== *Using the "TzHaar Fight Pit" [[Minigame Teleport]]. *Using the {{Fairycode|BLP}} fairy ring and running north. ==Monsters== The TzHaar Fight Cave pits adventurers against a succession of monsters, each harder than the last. The final boss is the powerful level-702 TzTok-Jad, but to get to him, players must battle past 6 other types of monsters ranging from level-22 up to level-360. The monsters are in order of appearance: {| class="wikitable" !Lvl !! Image !!Name !! HP !! {{plinkp|defence|pic=Defence icon}} !! {{plinkp|magic|pic=Magic icon}} !! Attack(s) !! Max Hit !! Notes |- |22 ||[[File:Tz-Kih.png|100px]] || [[Tz-Kih]] || 10 || 15 || 15 || [[Melee]] ||4 || Drains [[Prayer]] while [[Melee]]'ing; use [[Ranged]] or hit-and-run tactic to kill. |- |45 || [[File:Tz-Kek (level 45).png|100px]] ||[[Tz-Kek#Level 45|Tz-Kek]] || 20 || 30 || 30 || [[Melee]] ||7 || Recoils damage of 1 when attacked with [[Melee]]. |- |22 ||[[File:Tz-Kek (level 22).png|100px]] ||[[Tz-Kek#Level 22|Tz-Kek]] || 10 || 15 || 30 || [[Melee]] ||4 || 2 appear after a 45 is killed. |- |90 ||[[File:Tok-Xil (1).png|100px]] ||[[Tok-Xil]] || 40 || 60 || 60 || [[Ranged]], [[Melee]] ||13 || See the [[#Wave breakdown|wave breakdown]] for when to use [[Prayer]]. |- |180 || [[File:Yt-MejKot (1).png|100px]] ||[[Yt-MejKot]] || 80 || 120 || 120 || [[Melee]] ||25 || Can heal itself and other monsters that are below half their maximum hp |- |360 || [[File:Ket-Zek (1).png|100px]] ||[[Ket-Zek]] || 160 || 240 || 240 || [[Magic]], [[Melee]] ||54 || [[Ranged|Range]] with [[Protect from Magic]] on, and stay out of its [[Melee]] range. |- |702 || [[File:TzTok-Jad.png|100px]] ||[[TzTok-Jad]] || 250 || 480 || 480 || [[Magic]], [[Ranged]], [[Melee]] ||97 || See [[#TzTok-Jad|below]]. |- |108 || [[File:Yt-HurKot.png|Yt-HurKot|100px]] ||[[Yt-HurKot]] || 60 || 60 || 120 || [[Melee]] ||14 || 4 will spawn when TzTok-Jad falls below half HP. They will heal Jad if they are within melee range of it, or if they are in combat with the player and are within 4 tiles of Jad. Will sometimes heal themselves or adjacent Yt-HurKot that are below half hp if they cannot reach Jad. '''See the [[TzHaar Fight Cave/Strategies#Monsters|Monsters wiki page]] for techniques.''' |} ===TzTok-Jad=== {{Main|TzTok-Jad}} [[File:TzTok-Jad Animations.mp4|thumb|400px|right|Jad slams his feet to the ground for Ranged, and he rears up dangling his feet for Magic.|autoplay|loop]] At the final wave (wave 63), TzTok-Jad will emerge from where the orange Ket-Zek spawned and engage the player. Despite Jad's fairly low health, it is not to be underestimated - its attacks are immensely accurate and often deals massive damage, having a max hit of 95 for its magic attack and 97 for both melee and ranged, which can easily kill lower-levelled players in a single hit. Upon reaching 150 health points, Jad will summon four [[Yt-HurKot]] into the arena, who will make their way to it in order to heal it back to full health. If they successfully restore all of Jad's health before being killed, another set of healers will spawn when Jad reaches 150 hp or less health. ====Tactical analysis==== {{Main|TzHaar Fight Cave/Strategies}} ==Rewards== [[File:Fire cape detail animated.gif|frame|The fire cape]] If one is successful in defeating [[TzTok-Jad]], they will receive 8,032 [[Tokkul]] and the untradeable [[fire cape]] — one of the best melee capes in ''Old School RuneScape''. It provides much better protection than the [[Cape of Legends]] and the [[obsidian cape]], as well as slight offensive bonuses. The only strictly better melee cape is the [[infernal cape]], which is acquired from the [[Inferno]], a much harder version of the Fight Caves that requires sacrificing a fire cape to enter. Defeating TzTok-Jad has a 1/200 chance of awarding a pet [[TzRek-jad]]. This chance is boosted to 1/100 if TzTok-Jad is defeated while on a Slayer task. In addition, players may exchange a [[fire cape]] by speaking to [[TzHaar-Mej-Jal]] for an additional 1/200 chance of obtaining the pet. Tokkul is rewarded based on how many waves are completed, with each wave giving two more tokkul than the last. The total can be calculated as 2 + 4 + 6 + ..., or more simply N\times \left ( N + 1 \right ), where N is the number of waves completed. An additional 4,000 Tokkul are rewarded for killing TzTok-Jad.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Kieren|url=https://twitter.com/JagexKieren/status/847096840797523970|date=29 March 2017|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/105125|archivedate=6 November 2022|quote=Simple maths proofs: This formula is used for calculating your winnings from the Fight Caves :) Sum of n consecutive numbers}}{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Kieren|url=https://twitter.com/JagexKieren/status/847366350636957696|date=30 March 2017|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/107765|archivedate=6 November 2022|quote=Defeating jad gives you an extra 4000 on top of the normal reward too}} Rewards for completing the [[Elite Karamja Diary]] include doubled [[Tokkul]] from the Fight Caves and one resurrection per day inside the Fight Caves. ==Slayer== Killing TzTok-Jad can be unlocked as a slayer task for 100 slayer points at Duradel, Nieve or Chaeldar. Defeating waves 1-62 of the fight caves gives 11,520 slayer experience. Jad gives another 25,250 experience. Although optional, the four Yt-HurKot spawns can be killed on wave 63 for 60 slayer experience each. This totals out to 36,770 (up to 37,010) experience for all of the fight caves. ==Map & wave breakdown== [[File:Fight Caves Map.png|frame|A map of the TzHaar Fight Caves with some notable spots for safespotting and monster spawns.]] ===Map breakdown=== The TzHaar Fight Cave is mapped out on the right. Monsters spawn in waves, with each wave getting progressively more difficult. You can look below, under '''[[#Wave breakdown|Wave breakdown]]''', to see what monsters spawn in each wave. If you want to know exactly where the spawns are for the monsters on each wave, you can determine them based on the first two waves using the [[TzHaar Fight Cave/Rotations|Rotations]] guide. One of the main safespots is the '''''Italy Rock''''' (nicknamed after its shape) which is located on the eastern side of the arena. Standing directly on the western or southern wall of the Italy Rock will make the level 45 [[Tz-Kek]] and level 180 [[Yt-MejKot]] stuck on the corners. The Italy Rock is a great location to camp during waves where you encounter those monsters. The other two locations, '''''Long Rock''''' and '''''Dragon Rock''''', are also useful for safespots. Standing on the south side of the long rock or the west side of the dragon rock will lure all spawns to get stuck on them, except for the one that is immediately next to them. [[File:TzHaar Fight Caves safespot.png|thumb|300px|right|The player here is standing on the western side of the Italy Rock, keeping the Tz-Keks stuck on the corners.]] The Fight Cave does not have a single set of static enemy spawns. Instead, it has 15 [[TzHaar Fight Cave/Rotations|Rotations]], each with their own pattern of spawns. The current rotation can be determined based on the time of day or from the spawn locations in the first four waves. Spawn locations within a rotation do follow a cycle, though it is complex. Each rotation begins with a spawn at a particular point, then spawns future waves according to the following cycle (repeating indefinitely): SE, SW, C, NW, SW, SE, S, NW, C, SE, SW, S, NW, C, S. At the start of each wave, the highest-level monster will spawn at the next location in the cycle, with lower-levelled monsters spawning at subsequent locations in the cycle, going from highest-level to lowest. For example, in [[TzHaar Fight Cave/Rotations/12|rotation 12]] in wave 7, a ranger spawns at south-east, in wave 8 the ranger will spawn at south-west while the bat spawns at centre (the next spot in the cycle). In wave 9, the ranger will spawn at centre (the spot in the cycle after its last spawn location) while the two bats spawn at north-west and south-west. In wave 10, the ranger spawns in north-west, while the blob spawns in south-west, and so on. For TzTok-Jad specifically, he will always spawn in the same location as the first [[Tz-Kek]] (in wave 3) and the off-coloured [[Ket-Zek]] (on wave 62). For a complete breakdown of spawn points per rotation, see [[TzHaar Fight Cave/Rotations|Rotations]]. ===Wave breakdown=== The following table displays each wave the monsters will spawn. {{TzHaar Fight Cave Waves}} ==Tips== [[File:TzHaar Fight Caves safespot.png|thumb|The recommended safe area.|right]] * Going into wave three, wherever the Tz-Kek spawns is where Jad will spawn later on. Pay attention to this spawn point, and exit/restart to ensure that the Tz-Kek spawn point is on the south side of the "Italy" rock. This allows you to have protection to pot up before beginning the fight with TzTok-Jad. Alternatively, you can guarantee a beneficial rotation by waiting to enter the fight caves until a time that corresponds to the desired rotation, as the rotation is determined by the exact time when the player enters the caves and cycles every hour or so. A full list of the times and rotations as well as the current time can be found here [[TzHaar Fight Cave/Rotations]]. Jad spawns in this ideal location on rotations 2, 5, or 6. *Getting the 2+ Prayer boost at [[Edgeville Monastery]] or the Nature Grotto may be a help in the caves. **Alternatively, the [[ancient mace]] may be used before entering, preferably on a POH dummy with strength-boosting Prayers, equipment and potions for 20 or more additional Prayer at entry. It can be used on the [[Tz-Kek]]'s at the end of waves as well. *Especially in later waves (38+), you should stand in the north-eastern corner as 3 of 5 spawns get stuck that way behind Italy Rock and the other rock to the west. *Whenever killing a safespotted monster behind another one, kill the un-safespotted ones first, then immediately attack the safespotted one, as the death animation of the un-safespotted one will allow you to get a free hit on the safespotted one. **An exception to this is when using the level 45/22 Tz-Keks as a pseudo-safespot for [[Yt-MejKot]]. *'''You can REQUEST to log out of the game at anytime by clicking "Log Out" before you end your current round (when enemy NPCs are still alive).''' After you complete the wave, the wave will pause, you will log out safely, and the next wave will begin once you log back in. Upon logging back in, you will spawn in the middle of the room and will have 1 or 2 seconds to swap your prayer and run to where you want to be. This wave pause mechanic is useful for letting your [[Hitpoints]] regenerate in-between rounds. You can find a safespot, request a log out, let your Hitpoints regenerate and finish the wave knowing you will start the next wave after logging back in. **Note: if you fully log out before completing the wave (such as by clicking the logout button twice during the same wave), the wave you logged out during will restart when you log out and back in again rather than the next wave starting. *Prayer flicking [[Eagle Eye]], [[Hawk Eye]] or [[Rigour]] on the [[Ket-Zek]]s is useful for saving prayer. It is also advised to disable [[Auto Retaliate]] during the caves as the [[Tok-Xil]]s and [[Ket-Zek]]s can lure you out of safespots, thus allowing the Yt-MejKots to melee you. *Do not drink any [[Saradomin brew]]s unless you have to: if possible, wait until your Prayer is low, so you don't waste any prayer points from your [[super restore]] potions. '''Only a single dose of super restore is needed to restore combat stats after 3 doses of Saradomin brew. ''' *If possible, the [[Saradomin godsword]] is ''highly'' useful for completing the Fight Caves, as it restores both Hitpoints and Prayer, corresponding with the damage dealt. You can even safespot monsters while waiting for special energy to regenerate. If using the Saradomin godsword special attack on the level 180 [[Yt-MejKot]]s, it is advisable to get them down to half hp (39 or less to be safe) before using the special attack: this way they will use their own attack to heal, rather than to hit you. If using [[Void Knight equipment]], it may be useful to bring a melee helmet as well as ranged if you are using a Saradomin godsword as a special attack weapon. **The [[ancient mace]] can be used as a much cheaper, but less effective, alternative. *Using the [[regen bracelet]] allows you to heal 2 Hitpoints per minute versus one. Useful when safespotting or have monsters stuck behind rocks. *Using the [[Toxic blowpipe|Toxic Blowpipe]] has a chance to cause venom damage which will increase to 20 hit points. Useful for safe spotting the meleer or mager during the later rounds. ==Death mechanics== {{Safe death|IRS=yes|HCIM=yes|HCGIM=no}} [[Death|Dying]] results in the player respawning outside the Fight Caves with all of their equipment and inventory, their stats fully restored, and [[Tokkul]] awarded for each wave completed. After completion of the [[Karamja Diary#Elite|elite Karamja Diary]], once per day, upon reaching 0 hitpoints within the Caves, the player will be resurrected and can continue with the attempt. Dying in the Fight Caves does not cause the contents of an [[Item Retrieval Service]] to be lost. Dying in the Fight Caves does not result in {{Ironman|icon|mode=HCIM}} [[Ironman_Mode#Hardcore_Ironman|Hardcore Ironman]] players losing their Hardcore status. However, it does result in {{Ironman|icon|mode=HCGIM}} [[Group_Ironman_Mode#Hardcore_Group_Ironman|Hardcore Group Ironman]] players losing a life. Hardcore Group Ironman players can use the elite Karamja Diary resurrection without losing a life.{{CiteNews|url=https://secure.runescape.com/m=news/hardcore-worlds-are-coming-on-november-4th?oldschool=1|title=Hardcore Worlds Are Coming On November 4th|newsdate=22 October 2026|quote=Hardcore worlds will use the Hardcore Group Ironman ruleset for death{{nbsp}}[...] UNSAFE activities: TzHaar Fight Cave{{nbsp}}[...] safe: The Resurrection reward for the TzHaar Fight Caves from the Karamja Elite Diary}} The diary task list will display if the resurrection reward has been used that day. ==Collection log== The Tzhaar Fight Cave has 2 [[collection log]] items. The [[fire cape]] is guaranteed upon successful completion. {{Sync}} {{Collection log list|category=The Fight Caves}} ==Combat Achievements== {{Sync}} Switching worlds during any wave will render most of these combat achievements '''impossible''' to complete. Look at the individual achievement pages for more information. {{Combat Achievements list|TzTok-Jad|mobname=TzTok-Jad and the Fight Caves}} ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes
